interfaceCtat.descricao: Interface FIXA do tutor (a mesma tela para todos os problemas): enunciado; pergunta exibida "Nine sixths equals how many fourths?"; DUAS retas numéricas de 0 a 2, uma acima da outra: na Linha 1 a fração dada já está marcada pelo tutor; na Linha 2 o aluno digita em quantas partes iguais dividir (campo de denominador + confirmar) e marca o ponto da fração equivalente; à direita das retas, a igualdade entre as duas frações é mostrada em caixas: as da esquerda vêm preenchidas e, na da direita, o aluno digita o NUMERADOR (o denominador alvo já aparece); há também um seletor de comparação ("≟", "=", "≠") entre as duas frações; botão Hint; botão Done. Os passos do aluno são ações NESSES componentes (dividir a Linha 2, marcar o ponto, digitar o numerador, comparar, concluir).

componentes.papel: Linha 2 (versão sem rótulos) — o aluno divide e marca o ponto

Linha 2 — reta numérica com rótulos, onde o aluno divide e marca a fração equivalente
seletor de comparação entre as duas frações: "≟", "=", "≠"
campo numérico onde o aluno digita o NUMERADOR da fração equivalente
campo numérico do denominador da Linha 2 sem rótulos + botão de confirmar
campo numérico do denominador da Linha 1 (quantas partes) + botão de confirmar
campo numérico do denominador da Linha 2 + botão de confirmar
campo de texto do numerador exibido pelo tutor (não é do aluno)
imagem/rótulo do sinal de comparação entre as frações

dicas.texto: What does the denominator tell you about the equal parts in a fraction?
Look at the unit named in the question and use that number as the denominator.
The question asks for fourths, so focus on the number of equal parts named by "fourths".
Enter the number that tells how many equal parts make one whole when the parts are fourths.
The denominator tells how many equal intervals are needed between whole numbers.
Read the target unit, then enter that number in the denominator field for Line 2.
The target fraction is measured in fourths, so Line 2 needs four equal intervals for each whole.
Enter the number of equal parts required by the word "fourths," then confirm the division.
Equivalent fractions name the same amount, so both marks must be at the same position.
Use the marked position on Line 1 as the reference and locate the identical distance from zero on Line 2.
The mark lies halfway between 1 and 2, so look at the midpoint of that interval.
Drag or click the Line 2 marker at the point halfway between 1 and 2.
The numerator counts how many fourth-sized parts reach the marked amount.
Multiply the marked value by the number of fourths in one whole.
Use the marked value 1.5 and the denominator 4 in the multiplication.
Count four parts for one whole and two more parts for the half; enter the total number of fourth-sized parts.
Equivalent fractions have equal values even when their numerators and denominators differ.
Compare the locations of the two marks on the number lines before choosing a sign.
Both fractions point to the same position, halfway between 1 and 2.
Choose the comparison sign that means the quantity on the left has the same value as the quantity on the right.
Before finishing, check that both fractions describe the same point on the number lines.
Review the denominator, marked point, numerator, and comparison sign in order.
Confirm that Line 2 uses fourths, the marker is at 1.5, the numerator field contains the correct count, and the sign is equals.
After every field and mark agrees with the completed model, press the ... button once.

hints.message: Equivalent fractions name the same amount, so both marks must be at the same position.
Use the marked position on Line 1 as the reference and locate the identical distance from zero on Line 2.
The mark lies halfway between 1 and 2, so look at the midpoint of that interval.
Drag or click the Line 2 marker at the point halfway between 1 and 2.

hints.message: The numerator counts how many fourth-sized parts reach the marked amount.
Multiply the marked value by the number of fourths in one whole.
Use the marked value 1.5 and the denominator 4 in the multiplication.
Count four parts for one whole and two more parts for the half; enter the total number of fourth-sized parts.

misconceptions.description: O aluno responde com o denominador solicitado (4) no campo do numerador.
misconceptions.feedback: You entered the denominator as the numerator. The 4 tells how many equal parts make one whole; the numerator counts how many of those parts reach 1.5.

misconceptions.description: O aluno mantém a diferença entre 9 e 6 (que é 3) para a nova fração: x - 4 = 3 -> x = 7.
misconceptions.feedback: You kept the gap between the original numerator and denominator instead of preserving the value. Use the marked value 1.5 with four parts per whole.

hints.message: Equivalent fractions have equal values even when their numerators and denominators differ.
Compare the locations of the two marks on the number lines before choosing a sign.
Both fractions point to the same position, halfway between 1 and 2.
Choose the comparison sign that means the quantity on the left has the same value as the quantity on the right.

nodes.description: Click Done after checking the completed equivalent-fraction model.

hints.message: Before finishing, check that both fractions describe the same point on the number lines.

Confirm that Line 2 uses fourths, the marker is at 1.5, the numerator field contains the correct count, and the sign is equals.
After every field and mark agrees with the completed model, press the ... button once.
